parts: The box was sealed. The wallet was new.
And someone already had the keys.
Last week, Ledger confirmed it found an unauthorised hardware implant
inside a wallet sold through one of its authorised resellers in Southeast Asia.
On-chain researchers estimate up to ninety-three million dollars was drained,
from more than three hundred wallets.
It says its own systems and direct sales were not affected,
and every confirmed case traces back to that one seller.
If you bought from that reseller recently, don't set the device up.
If you already did, move to a fresh recovery phrase, on a device straight from the maker.
And no real company will ever ask for your twenty-four words.
Self-custody is only as strong as the path the device took to reach you.
Check the seal. Then check where it came from.
